title: A Wreath of Star Formation in NGC 7469
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 7469, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7469 · constellation Pegasus · about 220 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Armus, A. S. Evans

recognition.text: ESA/Webb Picture of the Month (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A spiral galaxy with blue-purple hues and orange-red star-filled regions spreads across this image, with a bright center crossed by a large star-shaped pattern. This is NGC 7469, a luminous, face-on spiral about 90 000 light-years wide, some 220 million light-years away in Pegasus. Its companion, IC 5283, peeks in at lower left.

The star shape is not a star. It is a diffraction spike pattern, made as light from the galaxy's bright core bends around the edges of Webb's hexagonal mirror segments and the strut holding its secondary mirror.

That core is an active galactic nucleus, blazing as gas and dust fall toward a central black hole. A ring of intense star formation circles it just 1,500 light-years out. Webb has found very young star clusters never seen before, warm turbulent gas, and signs that the nucleus is destroying small dust grains nearby.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.15 x 2.14 arcminutes) and distance (220 million light years), the frame spans roughly 138,000 × 137,000 light-years. Its light set out about 220 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image comes from Webb's NIRCam. Light at 1.5 micrometers is shown in blue, 2.0 in cyan, a 3.35-micrometer band that traces dust molecules in orange, and 4.44 in red.
understand.eye: This is infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the six-pointed spike pattern is made by the telescope rather than by anything in space.

explore: Highly ionized gas appears to be streaming out of the nucleus at about 6.4 million kilometers an hour, part of a known galactic outflow now seen in much finer detail.
The work is part of the GOALS program, which examines four nearby merging luminous infrared galaxies to learn about star formation, black hole growth and feedback.
alt: A face-on spiral galaxy in blue-purple and orange-red with a bright center overlaid by a star-shaped diffraction spike, with stars and galaxies in the background.
